In 1958 oil was found under the sea at Umm Shaif, off the coast of Abu Dhabi. Exports began in 1962 from Das Island, and onshore fields soon followed.

Abu Dhabi had been a poor sheikhdom of pearl divers and herders. Its ruler at first spent little of the new money, and in 1966 his family replaced him with his brother Zayed, who spent it on roads, houses, schools and hospitals.

Abu Dhabi holds most of the oil of the UAE, and its wealth was what made the federation work: it paid much of the federal budget. Dubai, with little oil of its own, took the path of trade and services instead.
